additional_concerns: Both permission claims contain stale uncertainty: footnote 3 is present at da12aecad4e68.u30.3569: “Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.” Its markers attach to XML and PDF, not the web form. The XML permission must retain this qualification.

The separately provided XML schema is absent. The XML obligation is established by da12aecad4e68.u14.2439, but actual schema conformity cannot be assessed. missing.xml_schema below identifies this missing authority; the packet does not identify which of its four opaque missing dependency IDs denotes it.
The four declared dependencies have null source_hash values and no substantive descriptions. Their availability or correspondence to particular requirements cannot be established.

The compliance candidates explicitly exclude XML schema conformity from their XML facts. This is consistent with a narrowly selected channel, method and e-Cert control, but TRUE must not be presented as complete XML submission compliance.

node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5 requires an e-Cert to be “supplied or used for this particular XML or PDF submission”. Footnote 3 establishes a certificate requirement but does not specify that operational manner. Certificate-use guidance is missing; the stronger interpretation remains unresolved. node.c8bd87cfd64bba8762d9b3a0 also delegates the substantive interpretation to an external classification.

node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 uses “date value 2026-02-02”, covering the pre-9:00am portion of that day. Other candidates use the operational launch. Preserve the tension between “With effect from 2 February 2026” and “following its implementation”; do not silently extend the resubmission trigger into the blackout.
The retained source supplies the 9:00am launch but no explicit governing timezone. Timezone authority and the treatment of the precise launch boundary remain unresolved.

The source permits urgent direct contact during the blackout; it does not establish that every contact constitutes an STR submission. Automatic migration likewise does not itself establish a new submission event.

The event candidates differ on whether a non-filing event returns FALSE or OUT_OF_SCOPE. This concerns the typed assessment domain, independently of these permission claims, and requires an explicit domain decision.
The history candidate detects the existence of a triggering event. A later resubmission does not erase that historical event; TRUE does not establish that a resubmission duty remains outstanding.
TRUE_IS_SATISFIED in the trigger candidates must be interpreted using their typed DUTY_TRIGGER questions. It must not be read as satisfaction or discharge of the resubmission obligation.
